This might seem good at first, but it's important to keep in mind that part of the design of the system is to allow the users to promote or suppress content democratically. The goal is to remove the burden on the maintainers of having to effectively be global site moderators, which is prohibitively time consuming and would essentially require full time staff.

People still have the option to promote good material and by not promoting bad ones, it is being suppressed, that right is not taken from them.

Exactly. Posts ranked relative to one another. Spam/etc are not going to be upvoted ever so downvoting them is going to do nothing - they'll be at the bottom whether that means +0 or -100. It's the same. What downvotes do do is enable people to suppress content that smaller minorities have expressed interest in seeing. If you have a post that has 10 upvotes, 10 people could then bury that post by downvoting it. As opposed to it being in the lower half or whatever, it's now dead.

And it's far from democratic. Something that happened with some degree of regularity on Reddit is that a post would be downvoted heavily by an agenda driven minority. Then somebody who actually liked it would gild the post. That gilding would bypass the normal ordering of the post (in other words - the bottom) and enable people to see it at which point it'd skyrocket. In other words the downvoting, given the absence of a way to "override" it, can enable people to avoid a democratic consensus on a topic.
